name: Shopify CSV Pre-Flight Checker — Fix Import Errors Before Shopify Rejects Your File
description:
Shopify rejected my product import and its error told me nothing useful — how do I find and fix what's wrong with my CSV? You fixed the file by guesswork, re-uploaded, and got rejected again — by the time you get the file into shape, you may as well have edited it by hand.
ShopifyCsvFix checks your product CSV the way the importer sees it, before you upload. Every problem comes back in plain language: what is wrong, and how to fix it. The mechanical errors are fixed for you, and the repaired file is re-checked, so you know before you upload — not after another failed import.
WHAT IT FIXES ON ITS OWN
- Column names Shopify silently ignores, renamed to the exact headers it expects (SKU → Variant SKU, Qty → Variant Inventory Qty, Price → Variant Price, Image URL → Image Src)
- Prices with currency symbols and thousands separators → plain numbers
- Float quantities (10.0) → integers
- yes / TRUE / no → true / false
- Messy tag spacing, and relative image URLs when your file's other images establish the domain
WHAT IT REPORTS — BUT NEVER SILENTLY CHANGES
- Duplicate variants (same handle + options): merging them is a business decision
- Variant rows missing an option value
- Prices that aren't numbers, and first rows without titles
VERIFIED, NOT VIBES
Seeded 5-row import file with 14 planted problems: 11 repaired (4 of them header renames the importer would have silently ignored), re-check confirmed the 3 real blocking errors, 0 new issues.
ONE-TIME $29, NOT ANOTHER SUBSCRIPTION
The big import tool in this category starts at $20/month — and its buyers complain about unexplained errors and a price that feels like a rip-off. This is a one-time $29 purchase, local and private: no upload, no store access, no subscription. Your full catalogue and pricing never leave your computer.
Windows 10/11, no other software needed. You get the repaired CSV + a plain-English fix report.
Scope: the CSV file itself. It can't see your store's existing products or settings — and it won't pretend to.
